term: 亚里士多德的动物观察
oneLiner: 第一次把动物系统观察、解剖并按形态归类，为两千年间的生物知识定下底本。
oneLinerEn: The first to observe, dissect and sort animals by form, setting the baseline of biological knowledge for the next two millennia.
detail: 他记述五百余种动物，按有无红血、胎生卵生、四肢与介壳等特征分层，已具分类学的雏形。他也提出「自然不做无用之事」的目的论解释，长时期主导后人对适应的理解。
detailEn: He described over five hundred species, layering them by the presence of red blood, live- or egg-birth, limbs and shell—already the skeleton of taxonomy. His purposive maxim 'nature does nothing in vain' long shaped how adaptation was read.

oneLiner: 以结扎与定量推算证明血液由心脏泵出、沿闭合回路循环，推翻了盖伦的千年血流成说。
oneLinerEn: By ligation and quantitative reckoning he showed the heart pumps blood around a closed loop, overturning Galen's thousand-year doctrine of the flow.
detail: 他算出心搏一次输出的血量远超餐食所能化生，若血液不回收则每日须制造数倍体重的血——唯一自洽的解释是同一摊血在体内循环。把定量推理引入生理，是生命科学方法论的一次跃迁。
detailEn: He computed that each heartbeat expels far more blood than a meal could ever generate; if blood were not returned, the body would make several times its own weight daily—the only coherent reading is one and the same blood circling. Bringing quantitative argument into physiology was a leap in method.

oneLiner: 自制显微镜看向软木薄片，第一次认出生命由一格格的「小房间」构成。
oneLinerEn: Peering at cork through a homemade microscope, he first saw that life is built of box-like little rooms.
detail: 他照样观察到蜂窝状小室，取拉丁文细胞之名命之；虽看到的只是死细胞的壁，却为「细胞是生命单位」这一观念埋下第一颗种子。稍后列文虎克用更利的透镜第一次看见活细胞与微生物。
detailEn: He saw the honeycomb chambers and named them cells after their Latin for 'little room'; though only the walls of dead cells, they planted the first seed of 'the cell is life's unit'. Soon after, Leeuwenhoek with sharper lenses first saw living cells and microbes.

oneLiner: 用属名加种加词的双名法，为混乱的动植物发下人人可查的「身份证」。
oneLinerEn: With genus plus species-name binomials, he issued every plant and animal a checkable identity card out of the earlier confusion.
detail: 他把界分为纲、目、属、种的层级，以生殖器官数简单归类植物，命名法却沿用至今。他的体系暗含「物种固定」的假设——而这份整齐秩序，很快就要被演化的思想松动。
detailEn: He split the kingdom into class, order, genus and species, sorting plants simply by the count of their reproductive parts—a naming scheme still in use. His system quietly assumed fixed species; that tidy order was soon to be loosened by the idea of evolution.

oneLiner: 第一个成体系主张物种会随环境改变而演化，尽管他给的机制后来被证伪。
oneLinerEn: The first to argue systematically that species change with their environment—though the mechanism he offered was later refuted.
detail: 他用「用进废退」与「获得性遗传」解释短颈的鹿如何一步步变成长颈：常不用的器官退化、常用的发达，且能传给后代。这一机制在达尔文之后被否定，但「物种可变」的洞见本身是重要的一步。
detailEn: He explained the short-necked deer becoming the giraffe by 'use and disuse' and the inheritance of acquired traits: unused organs waste, used ones grow, and both pass to offspring. The mechanism was refuted after Darwin, but the insight that species change was a real step.

oneLiner: 以自然选择解释物种的由来：变异、遗传与生存竞争的合演，无需设计者。
oneLinerEn: Explaining the origin of species by natural selection—the interplay of variation, heredity and the struggle for existence, with no designer needed.
detail: 他从家养选育推及野外：个体变异不均，资源有限致竞争，有利变异者留下更多后代，代代累积便成新种。华莱士独立想到同一机制，促使论文共同发表。这一理论把散落的博物事实收进一条因果主线。
detailEn: From breeding he reasoned outward to the wild: individuals vary unequally, scarce resources force a struggle, the better-fitted leave more young, and the accumulation across generations makes new kinds. Wallace hit on the same mechanism independently, forcing a joint publication. The theory gathered scattered natural-history facts onto one causal line.

term: 巴斯德驳倒自然发生说
oneLiner: 用鹅颈瓶证明微生物来自空气中已有的孢子，而非腐液自生，奠定病菌学说之基。
oneLinerEn: His swan-neck flasks showed microbes come from spores already in the air, not springing from broth itself—laying the base of germ theory.
detail: 鹅颈瓶能进气却拦落尘粒，瓶中肉汤久置不腐；一倾断颈，尘埃入内便生菌。生命来自生命（生源论）由此确立，也直接通向无菌手术、巴氏消毒与疫苗的路。
detailEn: The swan neck admits air but traps falling dust, and the broth stays clear for months; tilt and snap the neck and dust enters, and life appears. Biogenesis—life from life—was established, opening the road to aseptic surgery, pasteurization and vaccines.

oneLiner: 统计数万株豌豆的性状比例，悟出遗传是离散的「因子」按规律分离与组合。
oneLinerEn: Counting the trait ratios of tens of thousands of peas, he saw that heredity works by discrete 'factors' separating and recombining by rule.
detail: 高茎与矮茎杂交，子一代全高、子二代再现约三比一——性状并非融合稀释，而是由成对因子承载、随配子分离。这一超前的定量思路当世无人理解，直到 1900 年才被重新发现。
detailEn: Crossing tall with short peas gave all-tall first generation and roughly three-to-one in the second—traits not blended away but carried in paired factors that separate into gametes. This quantitative leap went unnoticed in his lifetime and was only rediscovered in 1900.

term: 摩尔根：基因在染色体上
oneLiner: 以果蝇白眼性状的伴性遗传，把抽象的遗传因子钉到了具体的染色体上。
oneLinerEn: Tracking the white-eye trait's sex-linked inheritance in fruit flies, he pinned the abstract hereditary factor onto the concrete chromosome.
detail: 白眼只随 X 染色体传递，与减数分裂中染色体的行为严丝合缝，基因因此有了物质载体。他又借连锁与交换率给染色体上的基因排定相对位置，画出第一张基因图。
detailEn: White eye rode with the X chromosome, matching exactly how chromosomes behave in meiosis, so genes gained a physical carrier. Linkage and crossover rates then ordered genes along the chromosome into the first gene map.

oneLiner: 两条链反向平行、碱基互补配对——遗传信息如何存储与复制，一眼看尽。
oneLinerEn: Two antiparallel strands with complementary base pairs—at a glance, how genetic information is stored and copied.
detail: 结构本身暗示机制：解开双链，各以互补原则配对新链，即为复制；碱基序列便是遗传密码。关键的一张 X 射线衍射图出自富兰克林之手，为模型定下螺距与直径，而这份贡献长期少被提及。
detailEn: The structure implied the mechanism: part the strands and each pairs a complement—that is replication; the base sequence is the code. The decisive X-ray diffraction image came from Franklin, fixing the helix's pitch and diameter, though her contribution long went under-credited.

oneLiner: 把成年乳腺细胞的核移入去核卵细胞，育出遗传相同的羊——分化原来并非不可逆。
oneLinerEn: Moving an adult breast cell's nucleus into a dewalled egg produced a genetically identical sheep—specialization, it turned out, is not locked in.
detail: 多利的基因组来自六岁母羊的体细胞，打破了「成年细胞命运已定」的成见，也开启了治疗性克隆与诱导多能干细胞的研究。它同时把克隆伦理推上公共讨论的前台。
detailEn: Dolly's genome came from a six-year-old ewe's body cell, breaking the dogma that an adult cell's fate is fixed and opening therapeutic cloning and induced stem-cell research. She also forced cloning ethics onto the public stage.

oneLiner: 三十亿碱基对的草图被读出，人类第一次拿到自身遗传的完整「参考书」。
oneLinerEn: A draft of three billion base pairs was read—the first full reference book of our own heredity.
detail: 国际协作测出人类基因组的参考序列，估定基因两万上下的数目，远少于预期，提醒复杂性状并非由基因数量简单决定。它把比较基因组学与精准医学的大门一同推开，也把「基因决定论」的误解一并摆上台面。
detailEn: An international effort read out the human reference sequence and set the gene count near twenty thousand—far below expectation, a reminder that complex traits do not track gene number. It flung open comparative genomics and precision medicine while laying the error of 'genetic determinism' bare.
